items.headline: Expert warns PM of unfixed state system flaws
items.summary: Cybersecurity expert Dr Sanjana Hattotuwa wrote to PM Harini Amarasuriya that weaknesses he flagged a month ago at LECO, the Health Ministry and Sri Lanka Police remain open. He warned they could expose payment records, health workers' IDs and confidential police complaints.

items.headline: Imported food prices may rise, minister warns
items.summary: Trade Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe said El Niño-linked weather in India could push up some imported food prices, though importers pledged to keep festive supplies flowing. Dried chilli shipments are held up over moisture limits, and the government says it will impose price controls if traders exploit shortages.

items.headline: Sri Lanka and Thailand talk FTA, visa-free travel
items.summary: Thai Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow met PM Amarasuriya at Temple Trees to push the bilateral free trade agreement. A memorandum signed on 22 November gives Sri Lankan ordinary passport holders 30-day visa-free entry to Thailand.

items.headline: Teen killed as car hits Kohuwala bus stop
items.summary: A 16-year-old from Nugegoda died after a car lost control on Monday evening and ploughed into a bus stop, also hitting several vehicles and injuring three others. The 68-year-old driver has been arrested.

items.headline: Idle Mahaweli lands to be taken back
items.summary: The government will reclaim Mahaweli land where approved projects have not started, Deputy Minister Aravinda Senarath said. Investors will get a grace period first, after which unused plots will be reallocated.

items.headline: Foreign Ministry budget head passed without vote
items.summary: Parliament approved the 2027 allocation for the Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Ministry at committee stage without amendment or a vote. The Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill also passed without a vote.

items.headline: Hakeem criticises block on Imran Khan debate
items.summary: SLMC leader Rauff Hakeem objected to a decision blocking a debate on former Pakistan PM Imran Khan, recalling Khan's role in Sri Lanka ending forced cremations during COVID-19.

items.headline: Teachers' union presses salary demands
items.summary: Ceylon Teachers' Union General Secretary Joseph Stalin said unions must keep reminding the government of teachers' pending salary demands.

items.headline: Govt seeks ways to catch income tax dodgers
items.summary: Senior Economic Adviser Duminda Hulangamuwa admitted many earners, especially professionals and traders, escape income tax. He proposed linking tax, customs, banking and land registry data, though no such system exists yet.

items.headline: Rs. 500m for northern power transmission line
items.summary: Funds have been allocated for early work on a 400 kV line from Kilinochchi to New Habarana, due by 2030, with US$150 million sought from the AIIB.

items.headline: First national battery testing centre opens
items.summary: A national battery testing centre built with a Rs. 161.5 million investment has been opened.

items.headline: Illegally assembled SUV seized, man arrested
items.summary: Police seized a jeep in Bandarawela that was allegedly imported without duty and assembled locally, and arrested a Gampaha resident in connection.

items.headline: T-56 and M-16 rounds found in Anguruwathota
items.summary: Police recovered 90 T-56 and 23 M-16 live rounds plus handcuffs hidden at Uduwara, acting on information from a suspect arrested on 20 November.

items.headline: Probe ordered into Kilinochchi Tank fish deaths
items.summary: Fisheries Minister Ramalingam Chandrasegar ordered an urgent inquiry after mass deaths of fish and prawns at the tank, with losses to fishing families to be assessed.

items.headline: Colombo–Kandy road reopens at Kadugannawa
items.summary: The Pahala Kadugannawa stretch reopened this morning after an overnight closure for maintenance.

items.headline: Heavy rain over 75mm in several provinces
items.summary: The Met Department expects heavy falls in parts of Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central and North Western provinces and Galle and Matara districts, with thundershowers after 2 pm. Rough seas and strong winds are likely around much of the coast.

items.headline: SL women face Ireland in Emerging Nations final
items.summary: Sri Lanka and Ireland both went unbeaten into the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy final in Ajman. Sri Lanka A also reached the ACC Rising Stars semi-finals after beating Bangladesh A by seven wickets.

items.headline: Hasina plans 16 December return to Bangladesh
items.summary: Ousted Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasina wants to fly home from India on the state carrier, despite Dhaka's vow to arrest her.

items.headline: Oil falls to three-month low
items.summary: Crude prices slid on higher Middle East supply and the restart of a Libyan pipeline.

items.headline: India to test all bottled water brands
items.summary: Indian authorities will test every bottled water brand after a sample from a leading brand was found unsafe.
